$comment: Vectors of the contributor page's ground guard, and every preset's background palette (ops decision D149 item 2; design CPAGE-REFINEMENTS-2026-10-15 §5; contributor-page-settings.v1 `theme.ground`, 1.1.0). The api runs the guard once at save, in C#, and the one builder writes the rows into contributor-page.v1 `theme.ground`; the edge renderer only checks the rows it is given. Each reads this file.

THE GUARD (`guard`). For an own colour `raw` and k = 0, 1, …, `steps`: mix raw toward white and toward black by k/64, each channel floor((raw × (64 − k) + white or black × k + 32) / 64), and take each mix's WCAG 2.2 contrast with the ink of its side (`inks.light` against the white-ward mix, `inks.dark` against the black-ward one). The first k at which either reaches `target` (7) decides; where both do, the side with the higher contrast, the light side on a tie. That side is the row's `mode`, and that mix its `ground`. `surface` is the ground mixed toward white by `surfaceSteps` of the mode; `ink` is the mode's ink; `muted` is the ink mixed toward the ground at the largest step m ≤ `mutedSteps` whose contrast against both the ground and the surface is at least `muted`, or the ink itself if none is; `rule` is the ground mixed toward the ink by `ruleSteps`; `focus` is the theme table's `focusRings` of the mode where its contrast against both reaches `focus`, and the ink otherwise (a safety net: with these inks and rings no colour reaches it). At k = 64 the light side is white, which reaches the target with the light ink, so the guard always ends. The inks are `purpose`'s own, `muted` is the theme table's `minimums.guard` and `focus` its `minimums.focus`: check:contributor-page holds all three to the table.

A CASE. `raw` is the input; `k` and `row` (contributor-page.v1 `$defs.groundRow`) are the answer; `note` says why a hand-picked case is here. The hand-picked cases give white, black, the six primaries, every preset's own ground, greys, the colours the design names, a case of each mode that stays as picked and one that moves, and neighbour pairs (one channel one step apart) whose k differs at the threshold and further along and whose mode flips. The cases `GS-001` onward come from `generator`: xorshift32 as the accent golden's, one draw per case, raw = the draw mod 2^24 as six lower-case hex digits. No case is decided within 1e-9 of a threshold, so the last bits of a pow function in .NET or in V8 cannot split one. check:contributor-page also runs the guard over every colour of a 16-step grid of each channel and holds each row to the renderer's figures (4.5 for text, 3 for the ring).

THE PALETTES (`palettes`). Per preset, in the schemas' order, five swatches beside the preset's own background (which is the settings' null, not a swatch): `id`, `label` and the rows. A swatch's row is the preset's own row of that mode with only the ground changed: `surface` and `rule` are derived from it as the guard derives them, and `ink`, `muted` and `focus` are the preset's own. `purpose`'s swatches are day and night pairs (`light` and `dark`), so a page with one still follows the visitor. `ratios` are each row's lowest contrast of the ink, muted, the preset's own accent and the focus ring against its ground and its surface, and of the logo's colour (#000000 on a light row, #ffffff on a dark one), rounded half up to two decimals. Every swatch reaches 4.6 for text and 3 for the ring and the logo, so a swatch never needs adjusting. contributor-page-settings.v1 `$defs.groundId` lists every id once.

THE DOCUMENT'S THEME (`themeCases`). For a `preset`, a settings `ground` (null, a palette id or #rrggbb) and an `accent` (null or #rrggbb): the `theme` the one builder writes into contributor-page.v1, and each ground's k. With a ground the accent is always present: the accent guard (the rule of examples/contributor-page-accent.v1.golden.json) runs against the ground's rows and the preset's print row, from the person's accent, or, where they chose none, from the preset's own accent for each row (on `purpose` its row of the same mode, otherwise its one row, and the print row's for print); `raw` is the colour the page's own row started from. Without a ground the theme is 1.0.0's.

`themeSha256` is the SHA-256 of the theme table's bytes these answers were computed against. When the table moves, regenerate with `node scripts/check-contributor-page.mjs --print-ground-golden > examples/contributor-page-ground.v1.golden.json` (it keeps the hand-picked cases, the palette grounds, the theme cases' inputs and the generator, and recomputes every answer and the hash), review the difference, and move every copy and pin in the same change.

cases.note: a strong blue: saved darker, a dark row (design §5.4)
a grey one step lighter than the web's mid grey
lavender: stays as picked, a light row
navy: stays as picked, a dark row
the ground of purpose by day
the ground of purpose by night
neighbour of the next: k = 0, a dark row
neighbour of the next: k = 16, a dark row
neighbour of the next: k = 23, a light row
neighbour of the next: a dark row
neighbour of the previous: the same k, a light row

themeCases.note: a purpose pair, the preset's own accents
a purpose pair with the person's accent
an own colour on purpose: one dark row, the dark accent lifted (design §5.4)
an own light colour on purpose: one light row
a swatch of a light preset
a dark own colour on a light preset: its accent mixed toward the dark ink
a swatch of a dark preset
a light own colour on a dark preset, with a person's accent
a swatch with the preset's own accent given as the person's
an own colour the guard moved
a swatch with an accent the guard moves
a grey the guard moved, on a light preset
no ground: the accent guard's answer of 1.0.0, unchanged
no ground and no accent: the preset alone
